syllabus_topics: Object-oriented programming with Java and C++.
Introduction to objects: definition; longevity; classes; methods; programs. Coding rules.
Operators, expressions and flow control in Java: precedences; assignment; operators; type conversions; literals; execution control.
Object construction: initialization and cleanup; constructors; overloaded methods; "this"; garbage collector.
Code organization: interface vs. implementation; libraries; member access.
Inheritance and composition: incremental development; "final"; class loading.
Enumerations; Exceptions; Collections; Input/output; Runtime type information.

Discussion and application of design patterns: Singleton, Null Object, Composite, State, Template Method, Strategy, Decorator, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Command, Observer, Visitor, Adapter, Façade, Proxy.
assessment_rules: For the normal period, a project accounts for 50% and requires a minimum grade of 9.5. Lab worksheets account for 50% and require a minimum grade of 9.0; only the 8 best of 9 worksheets are considered. Both components are mandatory for all students. The final grade requires a minimum of 9.5. For the special period, students may either reuse an approved Project or Lab Worksheet grade and take an exam for the other component, or complete a new project and an exam if neither component was approved in the normal period.
